title: Find the Value of the Partition
statement:
Split the positive integer array `nums` into two groups, `nums1` and `nums2`: every element goes into exactly one of them, and neither group may be empty. The value of a split is the absolute difference between the largest element of `nums1` and the smallest element of `nums2`, that is `|max(nums1) - min(nums2)|`.

Return the smallest value that any valid split can achieve.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every split costs O(2^n). Look at the answer differently: a split's value is the distance between two different elements (the maximum of one group and the minimum of the other), so it can never be smaller than the closest pair of elements in the array. And the closest pair is always reachable: sort the array and cut it between two neighbours; the left part's maximum and the right part's minimum are exactly those neighbours. In sorted order the closest pair is always adjacent, so the answer is the smallest gap between neighbours.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums` in increasing order.
2. Start `best` at `Infinity`.
3. For each index `i` from 1, compute `gap = nums[i] - nums[i - 1]` (never negative after sorting).
4. Keep the smallest `gap` in `best` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 3, 2, 4]` sorts to `[1, 2, 3, 4]`. The gaps are `2 - 1 = 1`, `3 - 2 = 1` and `4 - 3 = 1`, so `best` becomes `1` on the first gap and never drops below it. Cutting after `2` gives `nums1 = [1, 2]` and `nums2 = [3, 4]` with value `|2 - 3| = 1`. Return `1`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the scan is O(n).
- Space: O(1) extra besides the sort (the array is sorted in place).

## Pitfalls

- Sort with `(a, b) => a - b`; the default sort orders numbers as strings.
- Equal values are allowed, so the answer can be `0`.
- Only neighbouring elements need checking after sorting; comparing all pairs is O(n²).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `best` | smallest gap between neighbours seen so far |
| `i` | index of the right element of the current neighbouring pair |
| `gap` | difference between `nums[i]` and its left neighbour |

narration.2: Sort so that the closest pair of values ends up side by side.
narration.3: No gap has been seen yet, so start with Infinity.
narration.4: Visit each pair of neighbours, with i as the right one.
narration.5: The difference between neighbours is the value of cutting the sorted array between them.
narration.6: Is this cut better than the best one so far?
narration.10: The smallest neighbouring gap is the best split's value.
